decisions.evidence: Maker R4/entry7: paste box at top, card with 'fetched title, description, site, icon, and original address'. Client R4/entry8: 'a proper little card with the article's title, a short description, the site... and its icon'. Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-url + auto title/description/favicon + readable card. Partial: REF-BM-02 also names a preview image, which the maker's enumerated card never includes and which persists absent through the final app (entry109); client never surfaces it, but I fold this sub-field partial here rather than count it as a separate opportunity since the item is substantially present.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2/entry3 recaps goal (effortless save, find, read-later) omitting dedup and set-aside. Client R2/entry4: 'I also care about not ending up with the same link saved twice, and being able to clear out or set aside things I'm done with without losing them.' Specification stage.
decisions.note: Client proactively extends the asked-about goal scope with two reference requirements absent from the maker's summary: duplicate prevention (REF-BM-06) and reversible set-aside/archive (REF-BM-26). Both later built conforming (entries20, 71-78).

decisions.evidence: Maker R5/entry9 gate: 'does everything match your intent for the complete save-and-show flow?' Client R5/entry10: 'Opening it again... take me straight to the original page'; 'Fixing what got fetched... tweak the title or description — both right after saving and later'; plus re-raising dedup. Specification gate.
decisions.note: Extends the presented save-flow scope with two missing reference features: navigate-to-original (REF-BM-08) and edit auto-collected title/description before/after (REF-BM-03). Dedup (REF-BM-06) re-raised here but already counted at R2; not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R6/entry11 opens card to original in new tab. Client R6/entry12: 'clicking the card took me straight to the original article... opening it in a new tab so my library stays put is exactly the right call.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming build of REF-BM-08. In the same turn the client explicitly DEFERS judgment on dedup ('I'll hold my judgment on the don't-save-twice part until I can see it with a few links saved') — a pending clarification linked to and resolved at R10/entry20; recorded here in evidence, not counted as a separate opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Maker R9/entry17: edit title after saving. Client R9/entry18: 'I saved the article, hit the pencil, changed the title... and the card updated right there.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming build of in-place editing of fetched title/description (REF-BM-03/04). (A/B inline-vs-modal comparison at R7/R8 is a functionally equivalent UI choice, excluded as orthogonal.)

decisions.evidence: Maker R10/entry19: re-save existing url keeps count at 3 and opens existing card's editor. Client R10/entry20: 'instead of a fourth card... the count stayed at three and it jumped me right to the one I already had.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming build of duplicate detection (REF-BM-06). Resolves the R6/entry12 deferral.

decisions.evidence: Maker R12/entry23: '+ Add label', 'typography', pills on card. Client R12/entry24: 'Adding typography right there under the bookmark and seeing it sit next to design as little pills.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming assignment of one or more tags/labels (REF-BM-09). (A/B card-vs-editor placement at R12/R13 is equivalent UI, excluded.)

decisions.evidence: Maker R12/entry23 presents label-adding with no suggestions. Client R12/entry24: 'once I've used a label a few times, I'd expect it to start suggesting itself as I type... Can we make sure the label-adding includes that kind of suggestion?' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Client extends label-adding scope with autocomplete of existing tags (REF-BM-10), missing from the presentation. Maker agrees R13 and builds conforming at R14.

decisions.evidence: Maker R14/entry27: type 'typo', choose suggested 'typography'. Client R14/entry28: 'the typography suggestion popped up marked as an existing label... duplicate-resistant.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming build of tag autocomplete (REF-BM-10).

decisions.evidence: Maker R15/entry29 gate calls labeling flow (add/suggest/visible) complete. Client R15/entry30: 'I'd want to be able to take a label off a bookmark too, not just add them... click a little x on the pill.' Specification gate.
decisions.note: Client extends the labeling scope with tag removal (part of managing tags, REF-BM-04), absent from the asked-about scope. Built conforming at R16/entry31.

decisions.evidence: Maker R16/entry31: × on 'design' pill removes from this bookmark, keeps label available. Client R16/entry32: 'Clicking the × took design off this bookmark... still around to use on other links.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming build of per-bookmark tag removal (REF-BM-04).

decisions.evidence: Maker R17/entry33: type-as-you-go search across titles, descriptions, sites, addresses, labels, case-insensitive. Client R17/entry34: 'watching it narrow straight down... look across the titles, the descriptions, the site, the actual web address, and the labels... doesn't care about capitalization.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming plain full-text + case-insensitive search (REF-BM-12/13); tag search realized via label:/clickable pills (REF-BM-14 equivalent implementation). Partial: REF-BM-12's 'note' scope is absent because notes were never built; the client surfaces note-searchability separately (see notes extend).

decisions.evidence: First surfaced R17/entry34: 'once I can jot my own little notes on a bookmark, I'd expect those notes to be searchable the same way.' Re-raised R22/entry44, R47/entry94, and R54/entry108: 'I mentioned wanting to jot my own little private notes... searchable like everything else. I'd like that to make it into the real thing.' Disposition R55/entry109-110: maker defers notes; client: 'I'd like it picked up next cycle... it doesn't hold up what's in front of me.' Specification/implementation stage.
decisions.note: Client repeatedly extends scope with markdown/private notes (REF-BM-23) and note-searchability (REF-BM-12 note-component), absent from every presentation. Classified corrective/extend at first surfacing; the eventual disposition is an explicit, accepted deferral to next cycle (linked, not double-counted). caught=true — the requirement was surfaced and requested.

decisions.evidence: Maker R19-R21/entries37-42: click a label pill or the label row to filter to that tag's bookmarks, with a shared active state and 'show all'. Client R21/entry42: 'clicked design on the card and it narrowed to the design links... the organizing-and-finding-by-label piece feels complete.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming filter-by-single-tag (REF-BM-11). (card-pill vs toolbar A/B is equivalent UI, excluded; client wanted both.)

decisions.evidence: Maker R22/entry43 gate asks if the finding flow matches intent. Client R22/entry44: 'I wouldn't call finding finished... Exact wording — quotes... Combining conditions — design links but not accessibility ones, this word or that word... Mixing a typed word with a label.' Specification gate.
decisions.note: Client extends finding scope with exact-phrase (REF-BM-16) and boolean combining AND/OR/NOT + label+word (REF-BM-15), missing from the plain-search scope. Built R23-R27 via quotes, all/any toggle, include/exclude, label:+word. Partial: REF-BM-15's parenthesised nested groups (e.g. 'rome (#article or #book)') and the operators-must-be-quoted-to-be-literal rule are never realized (a global all/any toggle cannot express them) and never surfaced by the client; folded here as a noted partial of the same item rather than a separate opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Maker R23/entry45: '"design patterns"' returns only the exact-phrase match with an 'Exact wording' note. Client R23/entry46: 'gave me only Inclusive Design Patterns — not every link that happens to mention design and patterns somewhere apart.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming quoted exact-phrase search (REF-BM-16). (typed-query vs point-and-click A/B at R24/R25 is equivalent UI, excluded; client wanted both.)

decisions.evidence: Maker R30/entry59: 'Read later' button flips to 'In Read later', count rises. Client R30/entry60: 'flipped the button from Read later to a checked In Read later... the counter ticked up.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming mark-as-read-later/unread (REF-BM-17). (button-vs-icon A/B excluded as equivalent UI.)

decisions.evidence: Maker R32/entry63: 'Read later' tab/nav to a focused queue with only the NASA bookmark. Client R32/entry64: 'a clean view with just the NASA bookmark — the one thing I'd actually marked.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming separate unread view (REF-BM-18). (tabs-vs-sidebar A/B excluded as equivalent UI.)

decisions.evidence: Maker R34/entry67: mark NASA read → removed from queue, 'all caught up', still in All Bookmarks. Client R34/entry68: 'marking something read just clears it out of my to-read pile, it doesn't throw the bookmark away.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming mark-read-removes-from-unread while preserving the bookmark (REF-BM-19).

decisions.evidence: Maker R36-R39/entries71-78: Move to Archive removes from list, own searchable archive view, restore, and (R39) archived items excluded from everyday list/search unless searched inside Archive. Client R39/entry78: 'archived things genuinely stay out of my way until I deliberately go looking'; R38/entry76: 'Set aside, not lost... Restore clearly sent it back.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming archive-to-hide (REF-BM-26), reversible-vs-permanent framing (REF-BM-27), separate archive list (REF-BM-28), and the exclusion-from-default edge rule. (menu-vs-button A/B excluded as equivalent UI.)

decisions.evidence: Maker R40/entry79 gate calls the Archive flow complete. Client R40/entry80: 'I'd also want a way to genuinely get rid of a bookmark for good... In my head those are two different actions: set aside, I might want it later versus delete, I'm done with this for real... I'd expect a real delete to exist alongside archive, clearly separate.' Specification gate.
decisions.note: Client extends scope with permanent deletion (REF-BM-05) explicitly distinguished from reversible archive (REF-BM-27), absent from the presented archive scope. Built conforming at R41/entry81.

decisions.evidence: Maker R41/entry81: 'Delete permanently' with an irreversible named-confirmation, distinct from 'Move to Archive'. Client R41/entry82: 'archiving feels safe and reversible, deleting feels weighty and final... The two never blur together.' Prototype review.
decisions.note: Conforming permanent delete with confirmation (REF-BM-05). (delete-from-anywhere vs archive-first A/B at R42 is a behaviour choice; both delete, so equivalent on the reference item — excluded as orthogonal; confirmation-cancel R51 is beyond-reference robustness, excluded.)
